scope.purpose: Label an object with a short status or category word (Draft, Paid, Overdue), in a small colored box whose words carry the meaning and whose color reinforces it.
useCases: A status in a table cell, a list item, a card or a page header (Active, Pending, Failed).
A category or tag without valence (Beta, Internal) with the neutral intent.
A stronger signal with the strong appearance (a critical status that must stand out in a dense list).
An optional leading icon that repeats the status shape (check, warning) for faster scanning.
A count attached to a category with a trailing Counter (Bugs 12), in the badge colors.
exclusions: Selectable or clickable tags (filters): a later interactive component.
A dot without text: a later indicator.
Badges positioned over another element (avatar or icon corner): a later composition.
Badges inside a Button slot: a quantity in a Button is a Counter.
An accent or brand intent: open decision 2.
Live announcements when a status changes: the integration owns live regions.
alternatives: Plain text when the status is part of a sentence.
Alert (wave 3) for a message that explains the status.

fixtures: Phosphor glyphs re-exported by examples/icon/glyphs.ts for the leading icon examples.

checks.note: Schema, consistency, token coverage (38 paths) in 18 contexts and accepted components (--dependencies); check-foundations passes (384 roles, 1836 contrast checks, 0 failures).
1080 contrast records on the contrastScope backdrops in 18 contexts, 0 failures.

decisionsTaken: Colors from the approved color.status.{intent}.* family (surface, content, border, icon for subtle; surfaceStrong and contentStrong for strong) instead of a new indicator family: Badge is the status display the family was named for; the counter's colored emphasis stays deferred.

Foundations addition: color.status.neutral.{surface,surfaceStrong,content,contentStrong,border,icon} on the appearance axis, aliasing color.palette.neutral (light 100/600/800/0/300/600, dark 800/600/200/0/600/400), so that a category or a state without valence has a badge; four inventory contrast pairs added like the other statuses (content/surface 10.04 to 11.44, contentStrong/surfaceStrong 5.99, icon/surface 5.11 to 5.31, icon/surface.default 5.99 to 6.77; all 18 contexts pass). Brands inherit it through their palette.

Role names strongSurfaceColor and strongContentColor (suffix Color) because the role-type convention infers colors from surface, content, border or a Color suffix; the strong pair's contrast is guaranteed by the inventory pairs, not by the component report, which measures the subtle pair.
Leading icon at size.icon.xs (12 px) for every size: the indicator text is 11 to 14 px, so the 16 px icon of a sm Button would dominate; gap space.content.xs; optical placement like Button.
One line, truncated with an ellipsis when the width is short (table cells); the full label stays readable by assistive technology.
Strong appearance without a visible border (the strong surface already contrasts); the forced-colors edge is drawn in both appearances.
User review of the contract drafts (2026-10-16): a trailing slot accepting one Counter (Bugs 12).

Box: indicator typography (typography.indicator.{size}, 11/12/14 px), block size = line box + 2 x paddingBlock, cap-height centering, minimum inline size = block size, radius.indicator, padding-inline space.content.xs. The block padding exists so that a trailing Counter (whose box is the same line box) sits inside an even rim; every badge has it, so badges with and without a counter have the same height (md: 18.8 / 20.8 / 20.8 px in compact / standard / comfortable).

Foundations addition: space.content.2xs (density axis; compact 1 px, standard 2 px, comfortable 2 px: no 3 px primitive exists and 4 px made the comfortable badge as tall as a small control) for the badge rim; a generic role for the thinnest separations inside small content.

A trailing Counter takes the badge size and its content color; the inline padding on its side becomes paddingBlock so the counter is framed evenly. Counter needs no change: it already inherits the host color and size.

Trailing Counter only with the subtle appearance: measured in the 18 contexts, the counter digits on the 12 % tint reach 6.74:1 or more on subtle badges but only 3.95 (success), 4.33 (info) and 4.55 (neutral) on strong ones, below 4.5:1 for 11 to 14 px text. A strong badge with a count would need a counter without tint, which Counter does not offer.

openDecisions.question: Accept the foundations addition color.status.neutral.* (six roles, contrast pairs pass in every context) for the neutral intent?
openDecisions.proposal: Yes. Alternative: no neutral intent (status intents only) and categories as plain text.

openDecisions.question: Add an accent intent (New, Beta, brand categories)?
openDecisions.proposal: Not in v1: no status role carries the accent, and info already covers New. If wanted, add color.status.accent.* aliasing color.palette.accent (same six roles), which would also give Counter its colored emphasis later.

openDecisions.question: Dismissible (closable) badge: an option of Badge, or a separate Tag component later?
openDecisions.proposal: Recommended: a separate Tag component, scheduled with the filters and MultiSelect. A dismiss button makes the badge interactive (focus, keyboard Delete and Backspace, focus moved after removal, a dismiss event, a translatable Remove {label} name), and a status (Paid, Overdue) is never removable: only categories and filter values are. It also conflicts with the 44 x 44 px minimum target decided in the foundations: a 20 px badge cannot hold one without overlapping its neighbours, so Tag needs its own sizing (a taller box, or a documented exception to the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum of 24 px). If you prefer an option on Badge, I add dismissible, a dismiss part, a dismiss event and a dismissLabel prop in this wave, with those rules.

nextAction: Contract gate (grouped with IconButton and Link), second round after the user's review: reviewer confirms the trailing Counter, the neutral status roles and space.content.2xs (open decision 1), the scope without accent (2) and decides the dismissible question (3); then record the approval and start the implementation.
implementationNotes: Markup: <span class="ggb-badge" data-intent data-appearance data-size> with the leading icon (aria-hidden) and <span class="ggb-badge__label">; no role (static text). Truncation with native text-overflow and the full label in a title-free visually hidden copy only if truncation hides it (decided at implementation).
No Bits UI primitive (static content), like Counter.

informational.reason: The subtle badge edge is decorative framing: the label carries the meaning and reaches 4.5:1 on the badge's own opaque surface; WCAG 1.4.11 does not require a decorative boundary. color.status.*.border is a light tint by design (palette 300 in light, 800 in dark, 600 for neutral in dark).
